# COMA — Command & Communication for Autonomous Agents

> Machine-readable specification and RAG context index for ellmos-ai/coma.
> Updated: 2026-10-11 | Current package version: 0.3.2 (frozen).
> Install from the canonical Git repository. The PyPI name `coma` belongs to a different project.

## Scope

COMA coordinates jobs through local files and starts agent command-line tools as subprocesses. COMA itself does not implement a network service. A launched CLI may contact its provider or other services, require an account, and access the network. COMA does not sandbox child processes or block their network access.

The project declares no direct external Python runtime package dependencies in `pyproject.toml`. This describes COMA package metadata; it does not describe dependencies, permissions, or network behavior of agent CLIs, Python itself, or build tools.

## Core responsibilities

| Area | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| Job lifecycle | Create, execute, monitor, and retrieve jobs through a file-based board. |
| Session planning | Construct provider-specific argv without starting a process. |
| CLI adapters | Format arguments for provider CLIs; enforcement depends on the provider CLI. |
| Probe | Start a provider-specific reachability probe with a timeout and best-effort cleanup. |
| Starters | Generate `START.bat` and `start.sh` from a user-provided module manifest with a top-level `roles[]` array. |

COMA does not provide a scheduler, access-control system, lock manager, agent memory, provider account, or security sandbox.

## Job board protocol

The job board uses local directories such as `IN/`, `OUT/`, and `DONE/`. Callers must assign one writer per channel file. Optional role checks are not OS-level locking or identity enforcement and do not exclude two processes using the same role. Callers coordinate concurrent writes.

## Process and permission boundaries

Agent CLIs inherit the launching process privileges and environment. COMA does not request elevation or drop privileges. Configure and review each provider CLI permission profile and environment before starting it.

Adapter profiles differ. Claude `dontAsk` permits Read, Edit, Write, Bash, Glob, and Grep; its separate `read_only` preset limits tools to Read, Glob, and Grep. MCP is off by default; `bat_compat` can enable broader permissions and MCP. Codex defaults to `read-only`, `write` uses workspace-write, and `danger-full-access` can be configured.

Probe arguments are provider-specific and do not all establish read-only access: Codex adds `--sandbox read-only`; Claude adds `--strict-mcp-config` but no general read-only sandbox; AGY and Kimi add no access restriction. Inspect argv and CLI permissions before running. Kimi opt-in applies to adapter session planning and Spawner execution; `build_probe_command()` has no separate fail-closed guard.

On Windows probe cleanup requests process-tree termination; on Unix it kills the direct process. Cleanup is best-effort and descendant termination is not guaranteed.

## API and CLI

The public Python API includes `JobBoard`, `JobRunner`, `Spawner`, `ClaudeAdapter`, `CodexAdapter`, `AgyAdapter`, `KimiAdapter` (unverified; Spawner/session execution requires explicit opt-in), `build_session_plan`, `ordered_candidates`, `available_candidates`, `build_probe_command`, and `probe`.

Process planning builds argv only; Spawner execution starts the configured provider CLI.

Examples:

```bat
python -m coma --help
python -m coma adapters
python -m pip install "git+https://github.com/ellmos-ai/coma.git"
```

For role starters, provide a user module manifest with a top-level `roles` array and a prompt file for each role. Each role needs `id`, `prompt`, `request`, and a non-empty `providers` list. The prompt path is relative to the manifest and the file must exist. `ellmos-module.v2.json` describes COMA itself and is not a role-starter manifest.

```json
{
  "id": "my-module",
  "roles": [
    { "id": "reviewer", "prompt": "prompts/reviewer.md", "request": "Review the current change.", "providers": ["codex"] }
  ]
}
```

```bat
coma starters generate --manifest my-module.json --output-dir starters
starters\START.bat reviewer --provider codex --dry-run
```

## Known integrations

The following public repositories have documented, optional COMA integrations:

- [swarm_ai](https://github.com/ellmos-ai/swarm_ai) uses COMA Spawner and adapter APIs for provider-backed workflows.
- [marblerun](https://github.com/ellmos-ai/marblerun) uses COMA Spawner and adapter APIs.
- [ellmos-scheduler](https://github.com/ellmos-ai/ellmos-scheduler) uses COMA Spawner and adapter APIs.
- [task-master](https://github.com/ellmos-ai/task-master) has an optional COMA integration.
- [open-ocean](https://github.com/ellmos-ai/open-ocean) checks for optional COMA session support and provides a CLI fallback.
- [ticket-master](https://github.com/ellmos-ai/ticket-master) uses COMA Starters at build time; it is not a runtime integration.

## Related project

- [agent-ops-stack](https://github.com/ellmos-ai/agent-ops-stack) fetches seven repositories from its manifest and reports their declared wiring labels. COMA is a related project, not one of its manifest sources.

## Tests

The automated suite mocks provider CLI execution and does not perform live-provider verification. A probe test starts a controlled local Python process to check reachability. Test counts are available from current CI; this file does not pin a count.
